resources.string: Capture anything quickly. Find it later. Turn it into action when needed. Own your data.
This note already has that alias.
Other names for this note. [[Alias]] links here, and search finds the note by them.
Also the name of: %1$s. A [[reference]] to it will ask which note you mean.
A note can have up to %1$d aliases.
The file and its recognised text are removed from DROP. The note itself stays. Your original file elsewhere isn’t touched.
No app on this phone can open this file.
This file can’t be shown here. You can still open it in another app.
That backup file is damaged or incomplete. Nothing was imported.
That file isn’t a DROP backup. Nothing was imported.
Couldn’t read that file. Nothing was imported.
That file is too large to be a DROP backup. Nothing was imported.
This backup was made by a newer DROP (format %1$d). Update DROP, then try again. Nothing was imported.
Save all your notes, links and tasks to a file you choose, and bring them back later. Backup files are plain JSON and are not encrypted.
Couldn’t save the backup. Nothing was changed.
Importing only adds items that aren’t already in DROP. Nothing you have is replaced or deleted.
Import finished. Added: %1$d · Already in DROP: %2$d
You can undo this right away, or restore them from Trash later. Nothing is deleted permanently.
Tap Add notes to place notes on this canvas. Drag a card to move it; drag empty space to look around, and pinch or use the buttons to zoom.
Tap cards to connect them; tap a connected one to remove its line
Only the canvas and its card layout are deleted. The notes stay where they are.
A canvas lays out notes you already have as cards you can arrange and connect.
Couldn’t save. Your text is still here, so you can try again.
Drop a thought, or paste a link
“%1$s” and its rules are removed. The notes it showed are not changed.
Your changes to this collection haven’t been saved.
A collection is a saved set of rules. It shows the notes that match them right now and updates by itself. Notes are never copied or moved.
No notes match these rules right now.
No complete rules yet, so nothing is shown.
These rules were made by a newer version of DROP and can’t be shown here.
“Last edited” shows items whose most recent edit was this day; DROP doesn’t keep a history of earlier edits.
A few words about the day (optional)
Nothing was captured or completed on this day.
No open tasks. Today’s finished tasks are below.
Nothing logged today yet. Tap to add a few words about the day.
You can also add a task, save a link, record a voice note or scan paper from the buttons above.
No link on the clipboard. Paste one into the new note.
Notes and links you write appear here.
Task completed. It’s under “Completed today” in Tasks.
Times come from each task’s Resurface time.
Backup files contain your notes in readable form. Keep them somewhere private.
On Android 12 and later, a phone-to-phone transfer that you start yourself when setting up a new phone can copy DROP’s notes to it.
Your notes are excluded from Google’s cloud backup.
Everything you save is stored only on this phone, in DROP’s private storage.
If you uninstall DROP or lose this phone, your notes are gone unless you exported a backup.
DROP needs no account and has no internet access, so it never syncs or sends your notes anywhere.
Hidden. ECHO won’t suggest it for a while.

This suggestion has %1$s of %2$s possible points, shown as %3$d/100. Points come only from evidence in your notes: shared words (up to %4$s), the same project (%5$s), a connection on a canvas (%6$s) and a [[link]] (%7$s). Below %8$s points nothing is suggested; below %9$s it is shown as a possible match, because it rests on one kind of evidence. Everything is worked out on this phone.
Found by ECHO from shared words, projects and canvas connections.
Older notes related to what you edited recently, suggested by ECHO on this phone.
Found among your earlier notes, for you.
Share a page to DROP from your browser, or paste a link into any note.
Pin a note from its editor to keep it here, within easy reach.
Tap + to add one, or turn any note into a task from its ⋮ menu.
Every note as a Markdown file, with its attachments and a full DROP backup inside. Opens in any Markdown app.
DROP’s own format (version 3): keeps everything except attachments, history and the Vault, and imports back exactly.
Save it where you choose, or share it with another app. Markdown keeps formatting, aliases and properties; text keeps the words; PDF is for reading and printing.
To export one note as Markdown, text or PDF, use Export… in the note’s ⋮ menu. Projects can be exported from their own menu.
ECHO works on this phone only. This sets it on or off; you can change it in Settings.
Should DROP suggest related older notes?
If so, the Daily Log comes first on the Dashboard and the introduction shows the journal template.
If so, Save link moves forward.
Do you save links from other apps?
Reports, essays, documentation. If so, the introduction shows formatting, Focus Writer and History.
Handwritten notes, receipts, book pages. If so, Scan paper moves forward.
Do you capture things on paper?
If so, the introduction explains the Vault. Nothing is set up until you open it.
If so, the introduction starts with Resurface reminders.
Do you want notes to come back to you later?
Meeting notes, lessons, reviews. If so, the introduction shows templates.
Do you often write the same kind of note?
Sets the language of voice transcription. You can change it in Settings.
Which language do you dictate in?
You can change it any time in Settings.
If so, Voice dump moves forward among the capture buttons.
Do you like to dictate notes?
The quick-capture buttons are ordered for it.
Where do ideas usually come to you?

Only the note’s text is counted, not its title. Words are runs of letters or digits (“don’t” and “e-mail” count as one). Characters include spaces but not line breaks. Reading time is the word count divided by %1$d words per minute, rounded up.
No headings yet. Use H1, H2 or H3 in the formatting bar to add some.
“%1$s” is an alias of “%2$s” and also the name of: %3$s. References to it will ask which note is meant.
“%1$s” links to [[%2$s]], but no note has that title or alias. DROP never creates notes on its own; open the note to fix the link, or create the note yourself.
A rule in the collection “%1$s” refers to a project that has been deleted, so it never matches. Edit the collection’s rules.
This note has no title, text or attachments.
“%1$s” links to [[%2$s]], which is in Trash. Restore it, or change the link.
These notes share about %1$d%% of their wording. Nothing is merged automatically.
The value of “%1$s” in “%2$s” isn’t valid for its type (it may come from an edited backup). Open the note and set it again.
The canvas “%1$s” still has a card for “%2$s”, which is in Trash; the card is hidden until it’s restored.
The project “%1$s” still lists “%2$s”, which is in Trash.

These checks run on this phone and only read your notes. Problems are things that don’t work as you’d expect; suggestions are ideas you can ignore. Nothing changes unless you pick an action, and removing anything asks first.
Link that could mean several notes
Link to a note in Trash
Property value that doesn’t fit its type
Canvas shows a note in Trash
Project lists a note in Trash
It has no title, text or attachments. You can restore it from Trash.
Move this empty note to Trash?
The note stays in Trash; only its place in the project is removed.
DROP keeps the earlier version of a note when you edit it after a pause of %1$d minutes or more, up to %2$d versions per note. History stays on this phone and isn’t included in backups or exports.
− lines are only in this version; + lines are only in the current text.
The current title and text are saved as a version first, so you can come back to them. Only the title and text change: task state, reminders, projects, attachments and properties stay as they are.
Version restored. The previous text is in History.
This version is the same as the current text.
This note is too long to compare line by line. You can still preview and restore the version.
Notes, links and tasks: drop them here, find them later, and tick things off. Everything stays on this device.
To restore a DROP backup (.json), use Settings → Backup → Import.
Looks the same as a note you have
Choose .md or .txt files, or a .zip of them (like DROP’s portable archive). You see what will be added first.
No Markdown or text files were found.
Ticked notes are added as new notes. Notes already in DROP can’t be added twice; ones that look the same as an existing note are left unticked.
That file is too large to import.
That archive has too many files.
Enter a web address (example.com or https://…), an email (mailto:…) or a phone number (tel:…).
No app on this phone can open this link
No note has this title yet. DROP can create an empty note with it and link to it.
“%1$s” is in Trash. Restore it to open it?
No text was found. Clear, flat, well-lit photos of printed text work best. Handwriting is often not recognised.
Couldn’t read text from this file. The file itself is fine.
Read on this phone with Tesseract (English and Turkish). Handwriting is recognised poorly.
Reading the file again replaces the text you corrected.
Link: save a web address you copied or shared
Scan: photograph paper; its text becomes searchable
Voice: speak, and DROP writes it down
Tap a button on Home, share from another app, or use a home-screen widget.
Smart Collections and Knowledge Health keep a big library tidy without moving anything.
ECHO suggests related older notes and shows why, all on the phone.
Time Machine keeps earlier versions of your notes to compare and restore.
Your notes leave as Markdown, PDF or a full archive whenever you want.
The Daily Log keeps a short note for every day, next to what you did that day.
Idea Canvas: lay notes out as cards and connect them
Library: everything, with filters for tasks, links and pinned items
Projects: group notes you already have; nothing is copied
Search: finds words in your notes and in scanned text
Everything you save lands in one Library. Search finds words in titles, text and scanned pages; projects and canvases group things when you want.

So keeping it safe is up to you: export a backup file from Settings now and then. It holds your notes, tasks, links, projects, Daily Log and canvases. It doesn’t hold attachments (scans, PDFs, recordings), the text read from them, resurface times or Vault notes.
No account, no cloud, no ads, no tracking. DROP works offline and keeps everything on this phone.
Uninstalling DROP or losing your phone removes anything you haven’t backed up.
ECHO: points out related notes from shared words, projects, canvas connections and [[links]]. It matches words, not meaning, and runs on your phone.
[[Note title]]: link notes and see what links back
Resurface: choose when a note comes back to you
Notes are only useful if you find them again. DROP brings them back in three ways.
Start a note from a ready structure, or save your own.
Six built-in templates (meeting, study, project, journal, research, documentation) in the Library’s Spaces menu.
The Vault keeps notes encrypted with a passphrase only you know.
Vault notes never appear in search, ECHO, collections, backups or exports.
There is no way to recover a forgotten passphrase.
A quick place for your thoughts, tasks and links, on your phone and without an account.
The bar above the keyboard formats only what you select.
Focus Writer (⋮ in a note) hides everything else and shows an outline.
Headings, lists, checklists, quotes, code and links.
History keeps earlier versions if you change your mind.
Tip: Ctrl+K opens this on a keyboard. ↑ ↓ to move, Enter to run, Esc to close.
From your files. Up to 50 MB; text is read from the first 30 pages.
This PDF can’t be opened. It may be damaged or password-protected.
The file couldn’t be read. Try choosing it again.
Couldn’t save. Nothing was changed; you can try again.
Your phone is almost out of storage.
DROP can’t read this file. Choose a JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC or GIF image, or a PDF.
Keep a photo of a page, a receipt, a whiteboard or a PDF. DROP reads its text on this phone so you can search for it later.
After saving, DROP reads the text on this phone (English and Turkish). The original file is kept as it is.
Opens your camera app. No camera permission is needed.
How familiar are you with note apps?
Pick any, or none. You can change this later in Settings.
What will you use DROP for?
Vault notes are never exported. Importing only adds notes; nothing you have is replaced or deleted.
Tap Add items to bring in notes, tasks or links you already have.
Only the project is deleted. Its notes, tasks and links stay where they are.
A project groups notes, tasks and links you already have. Nothing is copied.
Typed details such as a status, a due date or a page count. Smart Collections can filter by them.
Enter a name of up to 40 characters.
Enter a value of up to 500 characters.
A note can have up to 30 properties.
Notes you asked DROP to bring back at a chosen time.
DROP will show you this note again at the time you choose. It’s a gentle reminder, not a task deadline.
In any note, choose ⋮ → Resurface… to have DROP bring it back later.
That note is no longer available.
Notifications are off. Resurfaced notes will wait in Resurface on the home screen.
Notifications are off for DROP, so resurfaced notes wait here instead.
Choose a time in the future.
Times are kept in your local time, even if you travel. Android may deliver them a few minutes late to save battery.

Backups contain your notes and tasks with their formatting, aliases and properties, plus links, projects, Daily Log entries, canvases, templates and Smart Collections. Attachments (scans, PDFs, voice recordings), the text read from them, resurface times, note history and Vault notes aren’t included; to take attachments with you, use Import & export → Portable archive.
Suggests related notes from shared words, projects, canvas connections and [[links]]. It runs only on this phone and never uses Vault notes or Trash. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Every earlier version of every note is deleted. Your notes themselves are not changed. This can’t be undone.
How note titles and text are shown in the editor. Your notes don’t change.
Your answers decide which quick actions come first on Home and which tips appear. Every feature stays available.
See which notes will come back, and when.
Transcription uses your phone’s on-device speech recognition when it has one, so your voice stays on the phone. Recordings you keep are stored only in DROP.
Only used when on-device recognition isn’t available. Your phone’s default speech service (for example Google’s) may send your voice to its provider. Off unless you turn it on.
Something went wrong while saving. Please share it again.
DROP can save shared text and links. This share didn’t include any.
This was very long, so only the first part was saved.
“%1$s” is removed from your templates. Notes already made from it stay as they are.
Your changes to this template haven’t been saved.
This is how the new note will look. Nothing is created until you tap Create note.
This template couldn’t be read, so no note can be made from it. You can still edit or delete it; your other templates aren’t affected.
None yet. Duplicate a built-in template, start a new one, or use “Save as template” in a note’s ⋮ menu.
Placeholders: {{date}} becomes today’s date, {{time}} the current time, and {{title}} (in the text) the new note’s title. Nothing else in a template is changed or run.
Share a page from your browser to DROP to save it, or tap Link to save a copied address.
Write [[Note title]] in a note to link it to another note.
Add a note to a project from the note’s ⋮ menu → Projects…
Scan printed pages: the text DROP reads from them becomes searchable.
Give a task a Resurface time from its ⋮ menu and it shows here as today or upcoming.

This item will be permanently deleted. This can’t be undone.
Items in Trash stay here until you delete them.
Your notes stay as they are. Only the passphrase that unlocks them changes.
All Vault notes will be permanently deleted. They don’t go to Trash and can’t be restored. Enter your passphrase to confirm.
Notes you add here are encrypted with your passphrase.
Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.
Something went wrong. Your Vault wasn’t changed.
Vault notes can’t be opened without the passphrase, and there is no way to reset it. The only option is to erase the Vault and its notes and start over.
The Vault locks when you leave DROP, turn off the screen, or after 5 minutes without activity.
Enter your passphrase to open your private notes.
It will be permanently deleted. Vault notes don’t go to Trash.
Couldn’t save. Your last saved version is still safe.
Private notes encrypted with a passphrase only you know. Vault notes stay out of search, widgets, backups and notifications.
I understand that a forgotten passphrase can’t be recovered
Vault notes are encrypted on this phone with a passphrase you choose. Without the passphrase, they can’t be read.
If you forget this passphrase, your Vault notes are lost for good. DROP can’t reset it, and neither can anyone else. Write it down somewhere safe.
Its file on this phone couldn’t be read. Your regular notes aren’t affected, and the Vault file is left untouched.
What you just captured won’t be kept.
The speech service lost its connection. What was heard so far is below.
Transcription isn’t available for this language on this phone. You can record audio instead.
Recordings stop after 30 minutes. Save this one, then start another.
The microphone couldn’t be used. Another app may be using it.
Nothing was heard. Try again a little closer to the microphone.
DROP needs microphone access to record. You can allow it in the phone’s settings; everything else in DROP works without it.
Couldn’t save. Your text is still here, so you can try again.
Your phone is almost out of storage. Recording stopped.
That recording was too short to keep.
Records audio only. Nothing is transcribed, and the recording stays on this phone.
This phone has no on-device speech recognition. You can record audio instead.
On-device speech for this language isn’t installed on this phone. Add it in your phone’s speech settings, or record audio instead.
Transcribed on this phone. Your voice isn’t sent anywhere.
Uses your phone’s speech service, which may send your voice to its provider. You allowed this in Settings.
Uses your phone’s on-device speech recognition. This Android version can’t confirm the language is installed; if it isn’t, DROP will tell you.
Tap Start and speak. Pauses are fine; press Stop when you’re done. The audio itself isn’t kept.
Connect one card to many in one go, add text blocks, and give cards a shape and a colour.
Each suggestion says why it was found and how strong the match is. Weak matches are called possible, never certain.
Opening a template no longer closes the app. Text, selections and dialogs stay readable on phones that darken apps by themselves. Headings and formatting now apply only to the text you select.
Pick a font for your notes in Settings. Setup can ask a few more optional questions, and you can change the answers in Settings at any time.
The Dashboard groups tasks into overdue, today, tomorrow and later. A task moved to tomorrow leaves today’s list, and the ones you finished today can be opened again.
Related notes appear on Home and under each note, each with its reason: shared words, a project, a canvas connection or a [[link]]. It all runs on your phone.
Tell DROP what you use it for in Settings → Personalization, and Home puts those actions first.
A short introduction explains what stays on your phone and what a backup holds. Open it from Settings.
Resurface also suggests older notes related to what you’re working on. Hide any you don’t need.
DROP 0.9.0: for people who live in their notes
Notes keep earlier versions as you write. Compare one with today’s text and restore it; the current text is kept first. History stays on this phone.

Save rules once and see matching notes update by themselves. Knowledge Health finds broken links, duplicates and forgotten drafts, and changes nothing unless you ask. Both are in the Library’s Spaces menu.

Export notes as Markdown, text or PDF, or everything as an archive with attachments; import Markdown with a preview first. Long-press notes in the Library to act on many at once. The Vault is never exported.
Start from six built-in templates or your own. Give notes other names that [[links]] understand, and typed properties like a status or a due date.

Headings, bold, lists, checklists, quotes, code and links from a bar above the keyboard, with undo and redo. Focus Writer (⋮ in a note) hides everything else and shows an outline, word count and reading time.
Capture a note or task in one tap
No notes yet. Tap + to capture one.
Open tasks you can tick off from the home screen
